note:
TRM and EBR test10k solve rates per k (unique training puzzles) and seed.

test10k is full-all rows 10,000-19,999; baselines/ebr/report.py sweep_official_rows() gives their official test rows.
TRM: score.right.npy holds one flag per official test row (422,786), so test10k is its mean over those rows.
  k = 1,000: baselines/runs/trm/sudoku-s<s>; other k: experiments/runs/trm/smalldata/n<k>-s<s>.
EBR: baselines/ebr/de1_report.py on baselines/runs/ebr/de1/n<k>-s<s>/score10k (evaluate.py on the same 10,000 puzzles), setting
  gtan0.2-cap64-N5 (the setting of the paper's main table); D64-N1 and D64-N5 are kept beside it.

  python data_efficiency_baselines.py   # writes ../results/sudoku-data-eff-baselines.json

With DE_VARIANTS=99: the 100-board runs, TRM in experiments/runs/trm/de2-v99/n<k>-s<s> (every k), EBR in
baselines/runs/ebr/de2-v99/n<k>-s<s>, k up to 100,000; writes ../results/sudoku-data-eff-baselines-v99.json.
FRM: baselines/runs/frm/de2-v99/n<k>-s<s>/runs/s<s>/test10k.json (baselines/frm/de2_adapter.py finish), every k.
DE_PARTIAL=1 leaves out runs that have not finished and records them under 'missing' (a preview export).
TRM at k = 30,000 makes 65,117 updates (E3-trm.sbatch EP = EI = 1,667: int(1667 * 30000 / 768); no epoch setting gives 65,100).
